newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin, French president meet at country estate.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin, French president meet at country estate.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, under pressure to show he is healthy enough to govern Russia, met French President Jacques Chirac on Sunday for his first talks with a Western leader since falling ill with pneumonia.

Interfax news agency said the meeting took place in the presence of only two aides, one French and one Russian, and an interpreter at the Novo-Ogaryovo residence outside Moscow. It was expected to last about two hours.
Yeltsin, dressed in a heavy coat and fur hat, greeted Chirac on the forecourt of the snow-covered estate after waiting for about a minute in temperatures of minus 18 degrees Celsius.
The Russian president smiled and looked in good humour but walked stiffly as he accompanied Chirac into the house.
"We are not only two European leaders but two friends," Yeltsin said. "It is unfortunate that you cannot stay longer but we will talk about the essential issues."

French television was allowed to film the initial greeting but barred from the meeting room. Yeltsin, who had heart bypass surgery in November, was discharged from hospital on January 20 after a bout of pneumonia. His opponents charge he is too ill to rule.
